title: Dedicated Throughput SLO – Proposed Contract / SLA Language (v1)
author: Sofia Mendes
body:
## Purpose
This page provides proposed contract and SLA addendum language for Redwood Dedicated throughput guarantees, including (i) the definition of the throughput service level indicator (SLI), (ii) measurement methodology and assumptions, (iii) exclusions/carve-outs, and (iv) service credits and claim procedure.

This language is intended to be incorporated into (A) the Master Services Agreement (“MSA”) as an SLA Addendum and (B) each Dedicated Order Form (or Order Form exhibit) that sets the tier-specific values.

> Note: This is a working draft for Legal + Product + SRE alignment. Do not send externally without Legal approval.

---

## 1. Proposed structure (how it appears in contract)
**Option A (preferred):** Dedicated Throughput SLA Addendum (standalone) + Order Form fields referencing this addendum.

**Option B:** Dedicated Throughput SLA section embedded into the Order Form exhibit.

Recommended attachments:
- Exhibit 1: Dedicated Deployment Description (region, shape, model set, tier)
- Exhibit 2: Dedicated Throughput SLO (this language)
- Exhibit 3: Support and Escalation (optional; references Support Policy)

---

## 2. Definitions (contract-ready)
**“Dedicated Deployment”** means a customer-isolated inference deployment provisioned under Redwood Dedicated, identified by a unique deployment_id in Redwood’s systems.

**“Tier”** means the Redwood Dedicated tier selected in the applicable Order Form (e.g., Standard, Performance, Premium).

**“Eligible Request”** means an inference request that (i) is received by Redwood at the Dedicated Deployment ingress, (ii) is validly authenticated and authorized, and (iii) complies with the Throughput Envelope (defined below). Eligible Requests exclude Customer Errors.

**“Customer Error”** means a request failure or degraded performance attributable to customer-provided inputs or customer-controlled systems, including without limitation: invalid parameters, unsupported model selection, exceeding token limits, network failures between Customer and Redwood, authentication failures, prompt formats that cause repeated runtime errors, or traffic patterns materially outside the Throughput Envelope.

**“Throughput Envelope”** means the bounded operating assumptions for which the throughput objective applies, as specified in the Order Form and/or Tier documentation, including: (a) model(s) covered, (b) maximum input context length and maximum output token limit per request, (c) request concurrency level or concurrency range, (d) streaming vs non-streaming mode (if applicable), and (e) region and hardware shape.

**“Output Tokens”** means tokens generated by the model and returned to Customer in the response body (including streamed tokens that are successfully delivered). Tokens are counted according to Redwood’s standard tokenizer for the applicable model version.

**“Effective Output Token Rate”** means Output Tokens divided by elapsed time, as measured by Redwood at the service boundary, computed per Section 3.

**“Measurement Window”** means the rolling time window used to compute Effective Output Token Rate. Unless otherwise specified in the Order Form, the Measurement Window is five (5) minutes.

**“Minimum Sustained Throughput” or “MST”** means the minimum Effective Output Token Rate (output tokens per second) committed by Redwood for a Dedicated Deployment, as specified in the Order Form for the applicable Tier, subject to the Throughput Envelope and the exclusions in Section 5.

**“SLO Event”** means a Measurement Window during which Redwood’s measured Effective Output Token Rate for Eligible Requests is below the MST.

**“SLO Compliance”** means that, during a calendar month, the percentage of Measurement Windows that are SLO Events does not exceed the SLO Event Budget defined in the Order Form (or, if not specified, the default objective in Section 4).

---

## 3. Measurement methodology (incorporation by reference)
3.1 **Measurement Standard.** The parties agree that throughput will be measured in accordance with Redwood’s “Throughput Measurement Standard” (currently identified internally as v1.0) as in effect on the Effective Date of the applicable Order Form (the “Measurement Standard”). The Measurement Standard is incorporated by reference into this SLA Addendum.

3.2 **Where measurement occurs.** Redwood will measure Output Tokens and timing at Redwood’s service boundary for the Dedicated Deployment (e.g., gateway / inference service layer), using Redwood’s internal telemetry.

3.3 **Effective Output Token Rate.** For each Measurement Window, Redwood will compute:
- Effective Output Token Rate = (Total Output Tokens successfully delivered for Eligible Requests during the Measurement Window) / (Length of Measurement Window in seconds)

3.4 **Aggregation and compliance evaluation.** Unless otherwise specified in the Order Form:
- Measurement Windows are evaluated continuously throughout the month.
- SLO Compliance is evaluated monthly.
- Scheduled Maintenance windows (as defined in Section 5) are excluded.

3.5 **Customer visibility.** Redwood will provide Customer access to throughput reporting (at least: Effective Output Token Rate and throttling/backpressure metrics) via Redwood Console and/or exportable metrics endpoints for the Dedicated Deployment.

3.6 **Recordkeeping.** Redwood’s measurements and logs will be the system of record for determining SLO Compliance, except in the case of manifest telemetry error materially affecting the calculation.

---

## 4. Throughput objective (template language)
4.1 **Commitment.** Subject to the terms of this SLA Addendum, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that each Dedicated Deployment achieves SLO Compliance for the applicable month.

4.2 **Default objective (if Order Form is silent).** If the Order Form does not specify the SLO Event Budget, the default objective is:
- SLO Compliance requires that at least 99.0% of Measurement Windows in a calendar month are not SLO Events.

4.3 **Tier values are set in the Order Form.** The Order Form will specify, per Dedicated Deployment (or per deployment group):
- Tier (Standard / Performance / Premium)
- MST (output tokens per second)
- Throughput Envelope (model(s), context/output limits, concurrency assumptions, streaming mode)
- Region and hardware shape
- Any tier-specific burst policy (if purchased) and whether burst capacity affects MST measurement

4.4 **Admission control and protection behavior.** Customer acknowledges that Redwood may enforce admission control, request throttling, queueing, or shedding behavior to maintain system stability and protect the Dedicated Deployment and/or Redwood infrastructure. Throttled or rejected requests that occur because Customer exceeds the Throughput Envelope will be treated as Customer Error and excluded from Eligible Requests.

---

## 5. Exclusions / carve-outs (SLO does not apply)
The throughput commitment does not apply, and SLO Events will not be counted, for any period of time or request impact attributable to:

5.1 **Scheduled Maintenance.** Scheduled maintenance communicated at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance, including reasonable emergency maintenance where advance notice is impracticable. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to schedule maintenance outside of Customer’s primary business hours where known.

5.2 **Force Majeure.** Any Force Majeure event as defined in the MSA.

5.3 **Customer Errors and non-Eligible Requests.** Customer Errors and other non-Eligible Requests as defined in Section 2.

5.4 **Customer-controlled systems.** Failures or performance issues caused by Customer networks, Customer systems, Customer-side load balancers, proxies, or any customer-managed components.

5.5 **Exceeding Throughput Envelope.** Traffic patterns materially outside the Throughput Envelope, including sustained concurrency materially above the stated concurrency range, or requests materially above token limits.

5.6 **Non-supported or Beta functionality.** Use of alpha, beta, preview, or “best-effort” features/models/hardware not designated as generally available for the applicable Tier in the Order Form.

5.7 **Security events and abuse.** Denial-of-service attacks, abusive traffic, or other security incidents requiring protective measures.

5.8 **Third-party provider events outside Redwood’s reasonable control.** Region-wide or provider-wide disruptions, provided that Redwood uses commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate (including failover where purchased/available under the Tier and deployment configuration).

---

## 6. Service credits / remedies (proposed schedule)
6.1 **Sole and exclusive remedy.** For failure to meet SLO Compliance in a given month (excluding the carve-outs above), Customer’s sole and exclusive remedy will be a service credit as described in this Section 6, unless otherwise required by applicable law.

6.2 **Credit eligibility.** Credits apply only to the monthly recurring fees paid for the affected Dedicated Deployment (or the portion of the monthly recurring fees attributable to the affected deployment), excluding one-time fees, professional services, and taxes.

6.3 **Credit amounts (proposal; Finance + Legal signoff required).** If Redwood fails to meet SLO Compliance for a month, Customer will be eligible to receive the following service credits:

- If SLO Compliance is met for < 99.0% but >= 98.0% of Measurement Windows: credit = 5% of the monthly recurring fee for the affected Dedicated Deployment.
- If SLO Compliance is met for < 98.0% but >= 95.0% of Measurement Windows: credit = 10%.
- If SLO Compliance is met for < 95.0% of Measurement Windows: credit = 25%.

Cap: total credits in a month will not exceed 25% of the monthly recurring fee for the affected Dedicated Deployment unless otherwise stated in the Order Form.

6.4 **No double recovery.** Credits will not be provided for the same underlying event if Customer is already receiving credits under another service level commitment (e.g., uptime) for the same month, unless expressly permitted in the Order Form.

6.5 **How credits are applied.** Approved credits will be applied against future invoices (not refunds) unless otherwise required by applicable law.

---

## 7. Claim procedure (customer-friendly but enforceable)
7.1 **Notice window.** To receive a service credit, Customer must submit a claim within thirty (30) days after the end of the month in which the alleged failure occurred.

7.2 **Where to submit.** Claims must be submitted via Redwood Support (or the designated enterprise support channel in the Order Form).

7.3 **Required information.** Claims must include:
- Customer name and account identifier
- Dedicated Deployment identifier(s) (deployment_id)
- The month of the claim
- A description of the observed issue and approximate time ranges
- If available, Customer-side request logs indicating request timestamps and whether streaming was used

7.4 **Investigation and response.** Redwood will investigate using its telemetry and respond within a commercially reasonable timeframe (target: ten (10) business days). If approved, Redwood will apply the credit on the next invoice cycle.

---

## 8. Customer responsibilities (conditions for guarantee)
Customer agrees to:
- Use the Dedicated Deployment in accordance with the Throughput Envelope.
- Follow Redwood’s published integration guidance for retries/backoff and streaming consumption.
- Not circumvent admission control mechanisms.
- Provide timely cooperation and information reasonably requested by Redwood to troubleshoot throughput issues.

---

## 9. Order Form fields (exhibit template)
Include a table in the Order Form for each Dedicated Deployment (or deployment group):

**Dedicated Throughput SLO Configuration (per Deployment)**
- Tier: [Standard | Performance | Premium]
- Region: [e.g., us-east-1]
- Hardware Shape: [e.g., 8xH100-80GB, 8xA100-80GB, 4xL4]
- Model Set and Version Pinning: [list]
- Streaming Mode: [Allowed/Required/Not used] (or “N/A”)
- Max Input Context Length: [# tokens]
- Max Output Token Limit: [# tokens]
- Concurrency Assumption / Range: [e.g., 32 concurrent requests]
- Measurement Window: [default 5 minutes]
- Minimum Sustained Throughput (MST): [X output tokens/sec]
- SLO Event Budget / Compliance Target: [default 99.0% windows not SLO Events]
- Burst Policy (if any): [None / Included / Purchased add-on] + parameters
- Reporting: [Console + export] (optional)

---

## 10. Notes for negotiation guidance (internal)
- Prefer setting MST and envelope assumptions in the Order Form rather than hard-coding numeric values in the SLA Addendum.
- Avoid committing to request/sec without strict request-shape constraints; tokens/sec is the primary measure.
- Keep carve-outs aligned with the Measurement Standard exclusions to avoid mismatch between Legal language and SRE measurement.
- Ensure Sales and Legal use consistent terms: “Minimum Sustained Throughput (MST)” + “Throughput Envelope.”
- If a prospect requests remedies beyond credits (e.g., termination right), route through Legal + Finance approval and document as an Order Form amendment.

---

## 11. Open items (before publish)
- Confirm whether SLO Compliance should be evaluated as “% windows meeting MST” (current) or as “p95 Effective Output Token Rate >= MST” (alternate). SRE preference is to keep window-based evaluation to align with error budgets and alerting.
- Confirm credit schedule and caps with Finance (Laura Bennett / Rishi Malhotra).
- Confirm language on failover and cross-region capacity (only if purchased / supported by tier and configured).
- Confirm whether throttled requests within the envelope are counted as Eligible Requests (current proposal: yes; throttling due to exceeding envelope: excluded).
